### **Job Description and Duties**

**Please note, the Water Boards do not participate in E-Verify.**

The Lahontan Water Board has an exciting employment opportunity in water quality protection. The Lahontan Water Board’s Nonpoint Source Unit has one opening for an Environmental Scientist (ES).

The incumbent ES will help protect water quality in the Lahontan Region by leading implementation of the region’s Nonpoint Source (NPS) Program. This includes NPS program management, Clean Water Act section 319 grants management, and implementation of permits and programs to manage impacts from rangeland and grazing operations.

Positions at the Water Boards may be eligible for a hybrid telework/in-office schedule based on the operational needs of the position. Applications will be accepted for individuals able to fulfill in-office duties from the Lahontan Water Board’s office in South Lake Tahoe.

Applicants should review the attached Duty Statement for more details about the position. Routine tasks include:

* Communicating with stakeholders, partners, and regulated entities
* Conducting meetings and field inspections
* Reviewing reports and tracking permit or project progress
* Data analysis and mapping
* Collaborating with other state and regional NPS programs
* Implementing outreach and education to the public, tribes, and regulated community
* Managing grants for projects to control NPS pollution
  

**Additional information:**

Candidates must possess essential personal qualifications including integrity, initiative, dependability, good judgment, the ability to work cooperatively with others, and the ability to perform the assigned duties of the class.

If the position requires driving, you must possess a current and valid driver’s license. Please Do Not include full Social Security Number, method of eligibility, and LEAP information in your application package.

Please let us know how you heard about this position by taking this brief survey: Recruitment Survey.

You will find additional information about the job in the **Duty Statement**.

**Positions at the Water Boards may be eligible for telework with in-person attendance based on the operational needs of the position****.**

**In accordance with the Statewide Telework Policy and GC 14200, the successful candidate must reside in California upon appointment. Proof of residency may be required.**

Employees appointed to this classification will have their monthly salary reduced and will accrue hours of PLP 2025 on the first day of each pay period in accordance with the applicable** **bargaining contract.** **The salary range(s) included on this job posting do not reflect the reduction in pay.**

jobs.title: Environmental Analyst
jobs.description:
Environmental Analyst
=====================

* Location: Richmond, California
* Program: Clean Water
* Type: Full-time
* Experience Level: Entry Level
* Salary: $82,500 to $87,500

Position Description
====================

* Posted: November 20, 2026
* First review of applications: December 7, 2026. For full consideration, please apply on or before the first review date.
* Application Close Date: The position will close on December 21, 2026 or when 125 applications have been received, whichever occurs first.

The San Francisco Estuary Institute (SFEI) is seeking an early-career scientist or engineer with an interest in environmental field studies and excellent organizational skills to join our interdisciplinary team investigating nutrient biogeochemistry and ecosystem responses in San Francisco Bay. This work will be carried out in support of the San Francisco Bay Nutrient Management Strategy (NMS; see https://www.sfei.org/programs/cw/nutrients), a research program that studies the impacts of nutrient loads on San Francisco Bay and evaluates potential management actions. Working with regional, state, federal and academic collaborators, we study the Bay’s biogeochemistry, water quality, and habitat condition using ship-based sampling, high-frequency in situ sensors, and coupled hydrodynamic-biogeochemical modeling.

This is a full-time position for a candidate who will play a key role in maintaining a network of water quality sensors and assist with data management and analysis. The candidate should have a Bachelor’s degree in a pertinent scientific field and familiarity with water quality, estuarine ecosystems, or a related area. They must be able to: (1) coordinate logistics and carry out boat-based fieldwork in an estuarine environment; (2) collect, review, and synthesize scientific data and information from various sources; (3) work well in teams as well as independently with general direction from senior scientific staff; and (4) communicate findings effectively in presentations, reports, and memoranda.

Primary position responsibilities will include:

* Contributing to the management of a distributed network of water quality sensors in San Francisco Bay.
* Coordinating, preparing for, and carrying out fieldwork on a boat.
* Occasionally lifting or carrying heavy field equipment for short durations.
* Servicing and calibrating water quality instruments in the lab.
* Assisting with maintaining telemetry equipment and troubleshooting issues with external partners.
* Conducting quality assurance and quality control (QA/QC) of NMS data and working with external laboratories to troubleshoot analyses and reporting issues.
* Assisting with project management and operations tasks for the NMS field programs (e.g., budget tracking, task management, and coordination with external collaborators).
* Assisting with writing technical reports and standard operating procedures (SOPs), and contributing to the development of posters and presentations for meetings and conferences.
* This position requires in office and/or in person presence at least 4 days per week for lab and fieldwork. Fieldwork may include 3-4 long field days (often early mornings) per month in varying weather conditions.

Qualifications
==============

Required Experience
-------------------

* Bachelor's degree in environmental science, civil or environmental engineering, oceanography, ecology, chemistry, biology, or a related field.

Required Skills
---------------

* Familiarity with environmental chemistry or environmental science.
* Strong attention to detail and organizational skills. Ability to manage competing priorities and adapt effectively in a fast-paced work environment.
* Experience with and/or the ability to lead or participate in boat or ship-based fieldwork, and to coordinate field and lab logistics.
* Ability to calibrate water quality instrumentation and conduct other lab-related tasks.
* Excellent communication, presentation and writing skills, and ability to synthesize information.
* Ability to work well in teams and work independently with general direction from senior scientific staff.
* Valid driver’s license.

Preferred Skills
----------------

* Experience calibrating and deploying aquatic instrumentation.
* Experience processing, analyzing, and visualizing data using Python or R (or similar).

Salary & Benefits Highlights:
=============================

* This will be an Environmental Analyst position. The anticipated salary range for full time employment is $82,500 - $87,500 for this position. Salary ranges take into account many factors for making compensation decisions including but not limited to experience, education, internal equity, and organizational needs. We expect to offer starting salaries at the low end of the salary range.
* Matching contributions to retirement plan (immediate vesting) (403B)
* Medical Insurance: health, vision, dental with employer and employee contributions
* 12 paid holidays
* Vacation days starting at 3 weeks accrual/year

About Clean Water
=================

SFEI's Clean Water Program provides the science behind water quality management in San Francisco Bay and the Sacramento-San Joaquin Delta. The Program is home to the Regional Monitoring Program for Water Quality in San Francisco Bay, which has tracked contaminants in the Bay for more than three decades, and to the Nutrient Management Strategy, which, since 2012, has built the monitoring, modeling, and synthesis capacity needed to understand how nutrients affect the Bay and to inform the regional Nutrient Watershed Permit. Clean Water staff work closely with the San Francisco Bay Regional Water Quality Control Board, Bay Area Clean Water Agencies, U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, U.S. Geological Survey, and academic partners.

==================================

Reserve

In-service title: Preventative Medicine Technician

As a part-time Environmental Health Assistant, you’ll be responsible for providing healthcare to support and maintain the health and wellbeing of Army members. You’ll work in and around Army camps minimising the risks posed by climate, non-combat injuries, unsanitary conditions and vector-borne diseases.

If you’re looking to experience adventure and excitement outside the everyday, earn tax-free pay and work as part of a close-knit team, this is an exciting opportunity that can work around your lifestyle.

### **What you'll do**

Your day-to-day

You’ll assist commanders in the prevention and control of disease and non-battle injuries to ensure ADF members can maintain a high level of health and fitness to carry out their duties.

Your training will equip you with the skills to study and assess environmental and occupational health threats, then implement effective control procedures.

Your duties may include:

* assessing environmental and occupational health threats by gathering and evaluating information obtained through health intelligence sources, on-site surveys and health surveillance
* determining and implementing counter measures to minimise the environmental and occupational health threats including vector/pest control, water quality analysis, food safety, waste management and sanitation
* conducting health surveillance and using health surveillance data to assess effectiveness of counter measures and plan investigations and health surveys
* conducting surveys and performing testing to assess environmental and occupational health threats and counter measures during deployment
* advising on the full range of Environmental Health Assistant issues to medical and non-medical personnel to help promote health and prevent casualties.

How you'll progress

Opportunities for progression and upskilling continue throughout your career. As you progress, the Army will provide you with development opportunities to assist you with your increasing leadership responsibility, as well as further education and specialised training to strengthen your skillset. This will help you to command and run a highly skilled team of soldiers and the employment of their equipment.

Where you'll work

The Army Reserve has units located all across Australia and offers you the flexibility to serve where you live. There are training locations in cities, small towns and regional areas. Even if there isn’t a unit close to you there may be other ways to serve. You’ll have a Careers Coach who you can ask about your options.

### **What you'll do**

Your day-to-day

You’ll be responsible for the planning, identification, evaluation and recommendations of control strategies to minimise environmental and workplace health impacts on ADF members.

In the field, you’ll ensure high environmental health and sanitation standards, that are appropriate for the situation you’re in. This may include not only providing advice but sometimes physically implementing control strategies (pest control, construction and maintenance of field hygiene facilities, etc). You may also be employed in disaster support, providing advice and support to deployed forces and affected populations.

Your duties may include:

* **advice to commanders –** combination of advice related to prevention of disease, active monitoring of environments, hazard management, and mitigation strategies and recommendations
* **human resource management –** managing Environmental Health Teams
* **water supplies –** providing advice on the safety and quality of all Army water supplies, including reticulated base supplies, field water supplies and swimming pools
* **food safety –** advising on the safety and quality of all Army food supplies including procurement, delivery, storage, preparation and serving
* **facilities –** determining that appropriate standards are applied to Army facilities to meet health and safety requirements and that facilities are being maintained in a sanitary and safe condition
* **work health and safety –** monitoring and evaluation of the Army working environment, providing recommendations for the control of workplace hazards including risk analysis
* **disease control –** implementing measures for the prevention and control of communicable disease and maintaining and interpreting disease statistics and other epidemiological data
* **waste disposal –** advising on the safe disposal of human, perishable and industrial wastes in accordance with compliance with appropriate environmental standards
* **pest control –** management and advice on the safe eradication of pests and vermin
* **vector control –** management and programs for the effective control of vector borne diseases
* **operational health support –** providing advice and preventative medicine services for hygiene and sanitation in field operations
* **disaster support –** maintaining public health standards in support of disaster preparedness and disaster recovery
* **liaison –** liaising with civilian environmental health and other specialist authorities.

How you'll progress

Opportunities for progression and upskilling continue throughout your career as an officer. As you progress, the Army will provide you with leadership, management, and specialist skills training to develop your ability to effectively manage your teams. We’re looking for a toxicologist to provide a written opinion on a novel mushroom ingredient used in dietary supplements. The opinion will support the review of an upcoming clinical study. This is a one-time project of about 1 to 2 hours, and all reading material is already prepared.

**What you’ll do**

* Review the ingredient documentation we provide
* Write a short, signed opinion on the ingredient’s safety for use in a clinical study

**What we’re looking for**

* A graduate degree in toxicology or a related field
* Experience assessing dietary supplement ingredients, botanicals, or fungi
* Clear, concise scientific writing

**Timeline**  
We need the completed opinion by November 25, 2026, so we’re reviewing applications as they come in.

**How to apply**  
Apply here with your CV and a line or two about similar work you’ve done.

Work Location: Remote

Environmental Analyst
=====================

* Location: Richmond, California
* Program: Clean Water
* Type: Full-time
* Experience Level: Entry Level
* Salary: $82,500 to $87,500

Position Description
====================

* Posted: November 20, 2026
* First review of applications: December 7, 2026. For full consideration, please apply on or before the first review date.
* Application Close Date: The position will close on December 21, 2026 or when 125 applications have been received, whichever occurs first.

The San Francisco Estuary Institute (SFEI) is seeking an early-career scientist or engineer with an interest in environmental field studies and excellent organizational skills to join our interdisciplinary team investigating nutrient biogeochemistry and ecosystem responses in San Francisco Bay. This work will be carried out in support of the San Francisco Bay Nutrient Management Strategy (NMS; see https://www.sfei.org/programs/cw/nutrients), a research program that studies the impacts of nutrient loads on San Francisco Bay and evaluates potential management actions. Working with regional, state, federal and academic collaborators, we study the Bay’s biogeochemistry, water quality, and habitat condition using ship-based sampling, high-frequency in situ sensors, and coupled hydrodynamic-biogeochemical modeling.

This is a full-time position for a candidate who will play a key role in maintaining a network of water quality sensors and assist with data management and analysis. The candidate should have a Bachelor’s degree in a pertinent scientific field and familiarity with water quality, estuarine ecosystems, or a related area. They must be able to: (1) coordinate logistics and carry out boat-based fieldwork in an estuarine environment; (2) collect, review, and synthesize scientific data and information from various sources; (3) work well in teams as well as independently with general direction from senior scientific staff; and (4) communicate findings effectively in presentations, reports, and memoranda.

Primary position responsibilities will include:

* Contributing to the management of a distributed network of water quality sensors in San Francisco Bay.
* Coordinating, preparing for, and carrying out fieldwork on a boat.
* Occasionally lifting or carrying heavy field equipment for short durations.
* Servicing and calibrating water quality instruments in the lab.
* Assisting with maintaining telemetry equipment and troubleshooting issues with external partners.
* Conducting quality assurance and quality control (QA/QC) of NMS data and working with external laboratories to troubleshoot analyses and reporting issues.
* Assisting with project management and operations tasks for the NMS field programs (e.g., budget tracking, task management, and coordination with external collaborators).
* Assisting with writing technical reports and standard operating procedures (SOPs), and contributing to the development of posters and presentations for meetings and conferences.
* This position requires in office and/or in person presence at least 4 days per week for lab and fieldwork. Fieldwork may include 3-4 long field days (often early mornings) per month in varying weather conditions.

Qualifications
==============

Required Experience
-------------------

* Bachelor's degree in environmental science, civil or environmental engineering, oceanography, ecology, chemistry, biology, or a related field.

Required Skills
---------------

* Familiarity with environmental chemistry or environmental science.
* Strong attention to detail and organizational skills. Ability to manage competing priorities and adapt effectively in a fast-paced work environment.
* Experience with and/or the ability to lead or participate in boat or ship-based fieldwork, and to coordinate field and lab logistics.
* Ability to calibrate water quality instrumentation and conduct other lab-related tasks.
* Excellent communication, presentation and writing skills, and ability to synthesize information.
* Ability to work well in teams and work independently with general direction from senior scientific staff.
* Valid driver’s license.

Preferred Skills
----------------

* Experience calibrating and deploying aquatic instrumentation.
* Experience processing, analyzing, and visualizing data using Python or R (or similar).

Salary & Benefits Highlights:
=============================

* This will be an Environmental Analyst position. The anticipated salary range for full time employment is $82,500 - $87,500 for this position. Salary ranges take into account many factors for making compensation decisions including but not limited to experience, education, internal equity, and organizational needs. We expect to offer starting salaries at the low end of the salary range.
* Matching contributions to retirement plan (immediate vesting) (403B)
* Medical Insurance: health, vision, dental with employer and employee contributions
* 12 paid holidays
* Vacation days starting at 3 weeks accrual/year

About Clean Water
=================

SFEI's Clean Water Program provides the science behind water quality management in San Francisco Bay and the Sacramento-San Joaquin Delta. The Program is home to the Regional Monitoring Program for Water Quality in San Francisco Bay, which has tracked contaminants in the Bay for more than three decades, and to the Nutrient Management Strategy, which, since 2012, has built the monitoring, modeling, and synthesis capacity needed to understand how nutrients affect the Bay and to inform the regional Nutrient Watershed Permit. Clean Water staff work closely with the San Francisco Bay Regional Water Quality Control Board, Bay Area Clean Water Agencies, U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, U.S. Geological Survey, and academic partners.

You’ll work in and around Army camps minimising the risks posed by climate, non-combat injuries, unsanitary conditions and vector-borne diseases.
